purpose.sources: Register the databases, files and services Provisa reads from, and set how each one is reached.
purpose.tables: Register a source's tables and set what each column is called, who sees it and how it is masked.
purpose.views: Define views: governed datasets computed from registered tables, read live or kept materialized.
purpose.relationships: Declare how tables join, so every query language can follow a link from one table to another.
purpose.metrics: Define metrics: named measures over the model that every query language can ask for.
purpose.commands: Define commands, the operations that write to a source or run code, and who may run them.
purpose.lineage: Trace where each column of a statement or view comes from, back to its sources.
purpose.dataProducts: Publish data products: owned datasets with the offers and contracts their consumers rely on.
purpose.team: Invite people into your organization and choose the role each of them receives.
purpose.roles: Define roles and the rights, domains and columns each one grants.
purpose.rls: Write row-level security rules that limit which rows of a table a role can read.
purpose.schema: Browse the model your role sees, as GraphQL SDL or as a diagram of tables and relationships.
purpose.nl: Ask a question in plain language and get it back as a query over your tables, ready to run.
purpose.graphql: Write and run GraphQL queries against the model as your role sees it.
purpose.cypher: Query the model as a property graph in Cypher and explore the result as nodes and edges.
purpose.sparql: Query the model as RDF in SPARQL and explore the result as a graph.
purpose.sql: Write and run SQL across every registered source, or compose a query on the table canvas.
purpose.grpc: Build and run gRPC calls against the protobuf service generated for your role.
purpose.jsonapi: Build and run JSON:API requests against the tables your role can read.
purpose.odata: See where an OData client connects, and read the entity sets this deployment serves your role.
purpose.openapi: Read the REST API's OpenAPI description for your role and try its operations.
purpose.explore: Ask an AI assistant questions it answers from governed data through Provisa's MCP tools.
purpose.python: Run Python in the browser against the data your role can read.
purpose.notebook: Work in a Jupyter notebook that reads the data your role can read.
purpose.contextHealth: See the health of the context layer at a glance, and approve the terms waiting for review.
purpose.glossary: Read the approved glossary terms, A to Z or by domain.
purpose.ontology: Edit the ontology: its classes, properties and concepts, and how they map onto tables.
purpose.contextMetrics: Read the metrics defined on the model. Metrics are edited under Model.
purpose.contextTags: Read the tags and the objects each one is applied to. Tags are edited under Admin.
purpose.contextClassification: See the kinds of data the profiler classifies and where each kind was detected.
purpose.contextSync: Keep outside catalogs and systems in step with Provisa, and see when each was last brought up to date.
purpose.requests: Approve, execute or reject the changes people have asked to make to the model.
purpose.welcome: Your organization is ready: invite people and connect its first source.
purpose.docs: Read Provisa's documentation, from the hosted site or the copy shipped with this install.
purpose.dashboard: See the model's counts and the health of each component of the deployment at a glance.
purpose.domains: Organize tables into domains and name the stewards who answer for each one.
purpose.environments: Create environments, copies of the model for development and test, and move changes between them.
purpose.cache: Set how query results are cached, and manage the materialized views kept for the organization.
purpose.triggers: Run a webhook, a SQL statement or a command automatically: on a schedule, when a table changes, or on a table's error.
purpose.federation: Choose and configure the engine that federates queries across sources.
purpose.orgEngine: See the engine lane and size your organization's queries run on.
purpose.email: Set the mail service invitations go out through, and the mail platforms sources sign in to.
purpose.maintenance: Turn the scheduled-downtime banner on before planned maintenance and off after it.
purpose.deploymentSettings: Read and change every operator setting of this deployment in one place.
purpose.platform: Declare the platform's regions and grant them to organizations.
purpose.regions: See the regions granted to your organization and the store it keeps in each one.
purpose.billing: See your plan, the current bill and the next charge, and move between plans.
purpose.observability: Follow your own query traces and see when telemetry last arrived.
purpose.platformObservability: Configure where the deployment exports its telemetry.
purpose.orgs: Create organizations, set their tiers and issue invite links.
purpose.aiModels: Choose the AI vendor and model for each assisted operation, and set the organization's API keys.
purpose.packageRegistries: Name the npm, PyPI, Go and Git registries that code sources install their packages from.
purpose.containerRegistries: Name the container registries that built images are pushed to.
purpose.sparkCluster: Set the Spark cluster a Spark script runs on by default.
purpose.classificationKinds: Define the kinds of data the profiler looks for, such as e-mail addresses or card numbers.
purpose.reports: Read the operational reports on the model, and add reports of your own.
purpose.security: Set the deployment's encryption and the providers people sign in with.
purpose.orgSecrets: Store the organization's secrets by name. A value goes in and never comes back out.
purpose.mySecrets: Store your own secrets by name, for the sources and keys you connect.
purpose.import: Import a Hasura v2 or Hasura DDN configuration into the model.
purpose.tags: Define the tags and tag categories that label tables, columns and other objects.
